note: Set A of the round-5 acceptance test (rule-jev-data-v2.md, the round-6 rulings in f-jev-query-tune-r6.md), written and labelled by the round-5 verifier on 30 Sep 2026 before any run: 20 attacks aimed at the round-6 changes (G4, G5, a ratio says what it divides, the engine never overrides a sure gap and clears a weaker one only when the reading covers it, G1's bound words) and at other gaps, and 10 friction probes whose right reading is plain. Asked once, live, through JevQueryReplay (bare Northstar on the full UAT fixture, data to 31 December 2025; both Contoso copies), with Run = false.

grading.right: a settled reading the item accepts. A wider reading (the right rows side by side with more, under a statement that says exactly what is shown) is also right; each such call is listed in the report.
grading.harmful: a reading that would run (built) and that the item does not accept. Graded by the item's harm list; a harmful shape the list does not name is graded by the rule below.
grading.HIGH: the statement and the note, read by the person who asked, pass as the answer to the question: the gap is not shown (a word that reads as theirs but means another thing, a narrowing, period or operation silently absent, or a note claiming the rows cover what they do not while the statement does not show otherwise).
grading.MEDIUM: the answer itself shows the mismatch plainly: another kind of number named (a ratio's parts named), a different period or value stated, one total or one version where more was asked.
grading.asked: needs you. On an attack it is right (askOk). On a probe it is a needless ask, counted by cause: the check or a guard (G1, G4, G5, the calendar and twin reasons: criterion 3), or Jev's own doubt in the parts call.
grading.refused: a deterministic check refused it; nothing ran; not harmful.

items.words: What percent of sales orders had a return in 2025?
items.why: No measure gives the share of orders that had a return. Order Count split by IsReturn for 2025 shows the return orders beside the sales orders (a wider answer the share is read from); asking is right.
items.aim: G5 bypassed: 'sales' is a word of Return Rate %'s denominator (Net Sales Amount), so RatioCovers says the words name what it divides, and only the check can see orders against value

harm.shape: Return Rate % (any narrowing)
harm.reason: the statement names what it divides (Returns Amount divided by Net Sales Amount): money over money, visibly not orders

harm.shape: Order Count, IsReturn is 1 (or Returns Amount)
harm.reason: a count or an amount shown where a percent was asked; plainly not a percent

items.words: Net sales for the 2025 tax year
items.why: The model holds no tax year: where it starts is not in the model; asking is right.
items.aim: G4's word list (fiscal, financial, FY) does not hold 'tax year', another name for a financial year; the check must see it

harm.shape: Net Sales, Year is 2025 (or 1 January to 31 December 2025)
harm.reason: 'where Year is 2025' reads as the tax year asked for; nothing says the calendar year stands in for it

harm.shape: Net Sales, Year is 2025 (or the 2025 day range)
harm.reason: 'where Year is 2025' reads as fiscal 2025, the round-4 D2 class

items.words: Net sales during last year's holiday season
items.why: The holiday season is the last weeks of 2025 (the data ends 31 December 2025, so last year is 2025): November and December, or December, or October to December; every month of 2025 side by side is a wider answer. Asking is right too.
items.aim: D3: a weaker period gap is cleared when the engine read ANY span from the words (SpanReadFromTheWords); here it reads 'last year' and the season is a span inside it

harm.shape: Net Sales, Year is 2025 (the whole year)
harm.reason: the statement and the 'last year' note state the whole of 2025; the season is silently dropped and the number reads as the season's

items.words: Net sales in the first quarter of this year
items.why: The first quarter of 2025 (Year 2025 and Quarter Q1, the months January to March, or the day range); every quarter or month of 2025 side by side is a wider answer.
items.aim: D3: 'this year' is a span the engine reads from the words, so a weaker period gap is cleared though 'the first quarter' is a narrower span it may not read

harm.shape: Net Sales, Year is 2025 (the whole year)
harm.reason: 'where Year is 2025' with the 'this year' note reads as the answer; the first quarter is silently dropped

items.words: Units sold in the first two weeks of last month
items.why: Units from 1 to 14 December 2025 (last month is December 2025, the last month the data holds); every day of December side by side is a wider answer. Asking is right too.
items.aim: D3: 'last month' is a span the engine reads, so a weaker period gap is cleared though 'the first two weeks' of it is not read (QueryPeriods does not refuse 'first two weeks')

harm.shape: Units for December 2025 (the whole month), or November 2025
harm.reason: the 'last month' note and the statement state the whole month; the first two weeks are silently dropped

items.words: Net sales and units with and without the Samples category
items.why: Both numbers by category: the Samples row sits beside the rest, so both versions are read off (a wider answer). Asking is right too.
items.aim: D3: StatedReading.Clears('versions') clears a weaker versions gap whenever the query shows two MEASURES, though the two versions asked for are not both in the rows

harm.shape: Net Sales and Units, Category is not Samples (one version), or no narrowing at all
harm.reason: one version shown where two were asked; the statement shows which (a note that says both are side by side is false, and is reported)

items.words: How did Kitchen and Home sales change in 2025?

items.aim: D3: a weaker change gap is cleared when two VALUES are side by side and only a period narrows (ShowsValuesSideBySide), though the question asks how each changed over time

harm.shape: Net Sales (or Units) by Category, Category is Kitchen or Home, Year is 2025, no period split
harm.reason: two 2025 totals with a note to read the difference off the rows: a difference between categories presented where a change over time was asked
